audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer built the entire matchup on a 'Pillar stun' and a 'Pillar wall': whys[2], spikes[0].text, spikes[3].text, mid, wants.you[0] and wants.you[2] all had Pillar of Flame stunning, slowing or walling off her exits. Two more errors sat on top: dontsFull[2] treated Defiant Dance as a shield that blunts your burst, and wants.foe[2] had her building Ionian Boots to 'dodge' the stun.
audit.why: Brand's W is delayed area damage with a 25% bonus against ablaze targets — no stun, no slow, no wall. His stun is Sear (Q), and only against a target already ablaze. Defiant Dance reduces physical damage during the charge, so it does nothing at all to Brand's magic damage. Tenacity shortens a stun; it does not dodge one. Irelia's actual sustain is Bladesurge, which heals her and refreshes on Marked or dying targets — Grievous Wounds is the answer, and the page never named it.
audit.corrected: Every Pillar-stun claim rewritten around E-into-Sear, the wave rewritten as the ladder Bladesurge climbs, and anti-heal stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer graded this HARD 8/10 with all seven chart rows given to Irelia, against a packet chart and a content chart that are both all-Brand and a 52.09% win rate over 407 games. The full-layer whys under those rows described Brand winning them.
audit.why: Bladesurge reaches 600 and Flawless Duet 850 against Brand's 1050 Q; her approach is what the E-into-Sear package is built to punish. She is dangerous once she is on you, which is a carry-threat problem, not a lane-phase one.
audit.corrected: All seven sides moved to Brand, difficulty regraded TRICKY 7/10 with her carry threat left at 8.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike carried a cooldown, and the level 3-5 spike was described through the non-existent Pillar stun.
audit.why: The real spike is level 3, when Conflagration can apply Blaze point-and-click so Sear becomes a guaranteed stun on a 600-range engage; her counter-spike is Flawless Duet at 16 seconds rank 1 and Vanguard's Edge at 125.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0].text, breakdown.cooldowns and the late paragraph.

audit.why: It is the field that carries the numbers.
audit.corrected: Flawless Duet 16s, Bladesurge's 600 range and reset condition, Vanguard's Edge 125s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Eighteen lintFindings: Irelia called he/his across tldr, tradeBad, phases[0].why, phases[2].why, breakdown.wave, breakdown.trading, dosFull[1].t, dontsFull[0].t, dontsFull[1].t, dontsFull[2].d and reports 0/3/4/8/11, plus dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d pasted from tradeGood/tradeBad.

audit.why: Vanguard's Edge's derived 'terrain' flag is genuine — Riot's text says the blades form a wall that damages and slows enemies walking through it. Brand's W 'terrain' flag is not, and appears to be what seeded the 'Pillar wall' error throughout this matchup.
audit.corrected: Wall language kept only for her R and removed everywhere it was attached to Pillar of Flame.

notes: Two separate defects here. First, the content layer credited Brand's W with a stun, a slow and a wall in six fields — Pillar of Flame does none of those; Sear is the stun and only on an ablaze target. Brand's W carries a bogus derived 'terrain' flag which is the likely seed. Second, the full layer graded HARD 8/10 with all seven rows given to Irelia against an all-Brand packet chart, an all-Brand content chart and a 52.09% win rate over 407 games; sides and difficulty are corrected as one group and no win[] twins were needed. Also corrected: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage only, so it does not blunt Brand's burst, and tenacity shortens a stun rather than dodging it. Bladesurge's self-heal and the Grievous Wounds timing were absent from the page.
